findings.title: load('sotus') returns a fitted CountVectorizer->LDA model, not the documented SOTU speeches (Drive id collides with 'nips_model')
findings.description: hypertools/io/load.py EXAMPLE_DATA maps 'sotus' and 'nips_model' to the SAME Google Drive file id '1J0MBhpRwdT2WChfWJ4HXYq6jU4XpyJPm' (lines 24 and 27). The shared payload is a pickled sklearn Pipeline (CountVectorizer(max_df=0.25, min_df=0.1, ...) -> LatentDirichletAllocation(n_components=50)), so hyp.load('sotus') hands scientists a fitted topic model instead of 'a collection of State of the Union speeches from 1989-2018' (load docstring). Local cache confirms: ~/hypertools_data/sotus and ~/hypertools_data/nips_model are both exactly 4101290 bytes; sotus_model is a different file (1886448 bytes). Every docs/gallery example that does hyp.load('sotus') and treats the result as text will break or silently do the wrong thing, and plot(corpus='sotus') text-fitting paths that load the raw corpus need re-verification. At least one of the two ids is wrong; the sotus text id needs to be restored upstream.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp; s = hyp.load('sotus'); print(type(s)); print(s)"
findings.expected: A collection of State of the Union speeches (text data), per the load() docstring
findings.actual: type: <class 'sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline'> | steps: [0] CountVectorizer(max_df=0.25, min_df=0.1, stop_words=[...]) [1] LatentDirichletAllocation(n_components=50, n_jobs=1)

findings.title: align() Returns docstring wrong twice: single array in -> list out (not 'same shape as data'), and claims manip 'ha[s] always returned arrays' (manip returns DataFrames)
findings.description: align()'s Returns section says: 'aligned : list of numpy arrays (or a single array) -- The aligned data, in the same list/single-item shape as `data` (matching `hyp.reduce`/`hyp.cluster`/`hyp.manip`, and the classic `hyp.align` API, which have always returned arrays).' Actual behavior: hyp.align(single_2d_array) returns a LIST of one ndarray (list[1]), not a single array; and hyp.manip returns pandas DataFrames (see finding 004), not arrays. Both documented claims are false as written.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; A=np.random.randn(30,5); out=hyp.align(A); print(type(out), len(out), type(out[0])); print(type(hyp.manip(A)))"
findings.expected: align(single array) -> single array per docstring; manip described accurately
findings.actual: align(single_array) -> list[1] of ndarray shapes=[(30, 5)]; manip(single_array) -> DataFrame shape=(30, 5)

findings.title: List-of-1 convention inconsistent: reduce/normalize collapse [A] to a bare array while align/manip/impute preserve the list
findings.description: hyp.reduce([A], ndims=2) and hyp.normalize([A]) return a BARE ndarray (the 1-element list is silently unwrapped), while hyp.align([A]) and hyp.manip([A]) return a 1-element list. Code written generically over datasets ('pass a list, get a list') breaks only for reduce/normalize with exactly one dataset, and align surprises in the other direction (single array in -> list out, finding 002). One convention should hold everywhere.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; A=np.random.randn(30,5); print(type(hyp.reduce([A], ndims=2)), type(hyp.normalize([A])), type(hyp.align([A])), type(hyp.manip([A])))"
findings.expected: Consistent list-in -> list-out (or consistent collapse) across all data functions
findings.actual: reduce([A]) -> ndarray (30,2); normalize([A]) -> ndarray (30,5); align([A]) -> list[1]; manip([A]) -> list[1] of DataFrame

findings.title: Return dtype split: reduce/normalize/align/analyze/apply_model return ndarrays; manip/impute/predict return DataFrames -- even for ndarray input
findings.description: Passing the SAME numpy array through sibling stages flips its type: hyp.manip(arr), hyp.impute(arr), hyp.predict(arr) return pandas DataFrames while hyp.reduce(arr), hyp.normalize(arr), hyp.align([...]), hyp.analyze(arr), hyp.apply_model(arr, ...) return numpy arrays (DataFrame input to reduce/normalize also comes back as ndarray). impute/predict document the DataFrame return; manip's docstring ('The manipulated data') does not, and align's docstring actively asserts manip returns arrays (finding 002). Chained user code (e.g. arr = hyp.manip(arr); arr[mask] += ...) hits pandas/numpy semantic differences silently.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; A=np.random.randn(30,5); print(type(hyp.manip(A)).__name__, type(hyp.impute(A)).__name__, type(hyp.predict(A, t=3)).__name__, type(hyp.reduce(A, ndims=2)).__name__, type(hyp.normalize(A)).__name__)"
findings.expected: One consistent output container convention (or type-preserving: array in -> array out)
findings.actual: DataFrame DataFrame DataFrame ndarray ndarray

findings.title: Data-arg named x in half the API and data in the other half; spec kwarg named after the function (reduce=/cluster=/normalize=) vs model= elsewhere
findings.description: plot/reduce/normalize/cluster/describe take their data as `x`; analyze/align/manip/predict/impute/apply_model take `data`. Model specs are `reduce=`/`cluster=`/`normalize=` on the classic functions but `model=` on align/manip/predict/impute/apply_model. Keyword calls that work on one function TypeError on its sibling. Verified: hyp.plot(data=A) -> TypeError "missing a required argument: 'x'"; hyp.reduce(data=A) -> "reduce() got an unexpected keyword argument 'data'"; hyp.manip(x=A) -> "manip() missing 1 required positional argument: 'data'"; hyp.cluster(data=A) -> unexpected keyword 'data'.
findings.expected: One data-arg name and one spec-arg name across the 1.0 API
findings.actual: x: plot/reduce/normalize/cluster/describe; data: analyze/align/manip/predict/impute/apply_model; model=: align/manip/predict/impute/apply_model vs function-named specs elsewhere

findings.title: normalize() validation raises AssertionError whose message lists 'none' as a valid value while the string 'none' is rejected; siblings raise ValueError
findings.description: hypertools/tools/normalize.py:240-242 uses `assert (normalize in ['across', 'within', 'row', False, None] ...)` with the message "scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer." Passing normalize='none' (the literal string named in the message) FAILS this assertion; only Python None/False are accepted. It is also an AssertionError (stripped entirely under python -O, and the wrong exception class for input validation), and the message names 'scale_type' -- a parameter name that does not exist in the public signature (`normalize=`). Every sibling raises ValueError with the pattern "unknown <stage> model '<name>'; supported names: ...". normalize is also the only stage kwarg that rejects the shared dict/class spec grammar entirely (documented, but a grammar divergence worth flagging: hyp.normalize(A, normalize={'model': 'ZScore'}) raises the same AssertionError).
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.normalize(np.random.randn(10,3), normalize='none')"
findings.expected: Either accept 'none' or do not name it as valid; raise ValueError naming the actual parameter and accepted values
findings.actual: AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: reduce()/plot() unknown-model error is a legacy message with embedded run-of-spaces and a pre-1.0 http:// docs URL, unlike the modern message its 6 siblings emit
findings.description: hyp.reduce(A, reduce='NotAModel') and hyp.plot(A, reduce='NotAModel') raise: "reduce must be one of the supported options or support n_components and fit_transform          methods. See http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html#hypertools.tools.reduce          for supported options." -- note the literal 10-space runs and the http:// link to the OLD module path hypertools.tools.reduce (1.0 moved reduce to hypertools.reduce.reduce; the linked page reflects pre-1.0 docs; URL currently 301s to https and resolves, but names the legacy API). align/cluster/manip/predict/impute/apply_model all use the modern pattern, e.g. "unknown align model 'NotAModel'; supported names: DeterministicSharedResponseModel, HyperAlign, ...". Same mistake, two different error grammars.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp\ntry: hyp.reduce(np.random.randn(10,3), reduce='NotAModel', ndims=2)\nexcept ValueError as e: print(repr(str(e)))"
findings.expected: "unknown reduce model 'NotAModel'; supported names: ..." matching the sibling functions, with a live 1.0 docs link (or none)
findings.actual: ValueError: reduce must be one of the supported options or support n_components and fit_transform          methods. See http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html#hypertools.tools.reduce          for supported options.

findings.title: Empty-list input: three different behaviors -- clean error (reduce/plot/cluster/normalize), text-corpus load + cryptic LDA crash (align/manip/predict/impute), silent empty return (analyze)
findings.description: hyp.reduce([]), hyp.plot([]), hyp.cluster([]), hyp.normalize([]) raise the friendly "ValueError: input has no observations (0 rows); there is nothing to plot or analyze." But hyp.align([]), hyp.manip([]), hyp.predict([]), hyp.impute([]) route the empty list down the TEXT pipeline: they print 'loading corpus: minipedia...done!' to stdout (on a fresh machine this DOWNLOADS the wiki corpus) and then crash with "ValueError: Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 1220)) while a minimum of 1 is required by LatentDirichletAllocation." -- a leaked sklearn internal that never mentions the real problem (empty input). hyp.analyze([]) raises nothing and returns []. Also related container inconsistency: hyp.reduce((A, B)) accepts a tuple as a dataset list, while hyp.align((A, B)) misparses the same tuple and raises "input has no observations (0 rows)".
findings.expected: All entry points reject an empty list with the same 'input has no observations (0 rows)' message, without loading any text corpus
findings.actual: reduce -> ValueError: input has no observations (0 rows)...; align -> [stdout: loading corpus: minipedia...done!] ValueError: Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 1220)) while a minimum of 1 is required by LatentDirichletAllocation.; analyze -> [] (no error)

findings.title: align/predict/impute silently swallow unknown **kwargs (typos and random_state= are accepted and ignored); manip raises TypeError correctly
findings.description: The **kwargs escape hatches on align/predict/impute forward to model constructors that accept and drop unknown keys: hyp.align([X,Y], model='SRM', totally_bogus_kwarg=123) runs clean; hyp.predict(X, t=3, totally_bogus_kwarg=123) runs clean; hyp.impute(Xn, model='PPCA', bogus_kw=1) runs clean. Concretely dangerous: hyp.align([X,Y], model='SRM', random_state=0) and random_state=1 both run without error and return IDENTICAL output -- a scientist believes they seeded (or set n_iter=, features=, etc. with a typo) when nothing happened. hyp.manip(X, model='ZScore', totally_bogus_kwarg=123) correctly raises "TypeError: ZScore.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'totally_bogus_kwarg'".
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; X=np.random.randn(40,6); Y=np.random.randn(40,6)
print(type(hyp.align([X,Y], model='SRM', totally_bogus_kwarg=123)))
a0=hyp.align([X,Y], model='SRM', random_state=0); a1=hyp.align([X,Y], model='SRM', random_state=1)
print('differ:', not all(np.array_equal(p,q) for p,q in zip(a0,a1)))"
findings.expected: Unknown constructor kwargs raise TypeError naming the bad key (as manip does)
findings.actual: align bogus kwarg: NO ERROR; predict bogus kwarg: NO ERROR; impute PPCA bogus kwarg: NO ERROR; SRM random_state 0 vs 1 differ: False

findings.title: random_state parameter exists only on plot/analyze/reduce/cluster; align/manip/predict/impute/apply_model have no seed path
findings.description: plot, analyze, reduce, and cluster expose random_state= (documented as injected into any stage model accepting it). align, manip, predict, impute, and apply_model have no random_state parameter at all -- and for align/predict/impute the **kwargs fallback silently ignores one (finding 009), so there is NO working way to seed e.g. a probabilistic SRM or a stochastic imputer through the public API short of constructing the model instance yourself. For a library pitching reproducible science, the seed surface is half-covered.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import inspect, hypertools as hyp; print({f.__name__: 'random_state' in inspect.signature(f).parameters for f in [hyp.plot, hyp.analyze, hyp.reduce, hyp.cluster, hyp.align, hyp.manip, hyp.predict, hyp.impute, hyp.apply_model]})"
findings.expected: random_state supported (or explicitly documented as unsupported) uniformly
findings.actual: {'plot': True, 'analyze': True, 'reduce': True, 'cluster': True, 'align': False, 'manip': False, 'predict': False, 'impute': False, 'apply_model': False}

findings.title: save(obj, fname, **kwargs) accepts arbitrary kwargs and silently drops them; docstring is a bare one-liner
findings.description: hypertools/io/save.py: `def save(obj, fname, **kwargs): "Pickle obj to fname." with open(fname, 'wb') as f: pickle.dump(obj, f)`. Any kwarg -- e.g. hyp.save(A, path, protocol=5) or a typo'd fname kwarg -- is accepted and ignored (pickle.dump never sees it). The docstring has no Parameters/Returns section, no mention that the format is always pickle regardless of extension, and no pointer to the load() security warning about pickles. Every other public function has full numpydoc.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp, tempfile, os; p=os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(),'x1.pkl'); hyp.save(np.eye(3), p, protocol=999, bogus=1); print('no error; kwargs dropped'); os.remove(p)"
findings.expected: TypeError on unknown kwargs (protocol=999 is invalid and should fail), or kwargs forwarded to pickle.dump; a real docstring
findings.actual: no error; kwargs dropped (pickle.dump called without them; source: 'def save(obj, fname, **kwargs): ... pickle.dump(obj, f)')

findings.title: describe(): max_dims is an exclusive bound starting at 2 (max_dims=6 tests dims 2-5); 'average' key is the stacked-data curve, not the average of 'individual'; unconditional slow-warning
findings.description: describe()'s public docstring says max_dims is the 'Maximum number of dimensions to consider', but the implementation iterates `range(2, max_dims)` (describe.py:110), so the named maximum is never computed and dim 1 is never tested: describe(x, max_dims=6) returns 4 correlations (dims 2,3,4,5). The result key 'average' is documented as 'the correlation by number of components for all data' but is computed by STACKING all datasets (np.vstack) and correlating once -- verified numerically that result['average'] != mean(result['individual']) (allclose False on a 2-dataset run), so the key name misleads. describe() also emits warnings.warn('When input data is large, this computation can take a long time.') unconditionally on every call, even for a 50x8 array.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; D=[np.random.default_rng(i).standard_normal((50,8)) for i in (1,2)]; r=hyp.describe(D, show=False, max_dims=6); print(len(r['average'])); import numpy as np; print(np.allclose(np.asarray(r['average']), np.mean(np.stack([np.asarray(v) for v in r['individual']]), axis=0)))"
findings.expected: max_dims=6 -> correlations for up to 6 dims; 'average' = average of individual curves (or renamed/documented as 'stacked')
findings.actual: len(result['average']) == 4 for max_dims=6; average == mean(individual) -> False

findings.title: load() docstring: 'spiral is numpy array' -- actually a list of two (1000, 3) arrays

findings.title: Census: no __all__; star-import and dir() expose internal modules -- datageometry (self-described INTERNAL), external (vendored), tools (legacy), config (leaks importlib.metadata.version), core (un-underscored internals)
findings.description: hypertools defines no __all__, so `from hypertools import *` imports 22 names including the submodules config, core, datageometry, external, io, tools. hypertools.datageometry's own module docstring begins 'INTERNAL -- not part of the public API' yet it sits in the top-level namespace. hypertools.external exposes vendored ppca/brainiak code (module docstring: 'Vendored third-party algorithms'); the project CLAUDE.md calls this package `hypertools/_externals/` but the real package has no underscore. hypertools.config.version is the raw importlib.metadata.version FUNCTION (calling hyp.config.version() -> TypeError missing 'distribution_name'), sitting next to __version__. hypertools.core exposes RobustDict, apply_defaults, get, build_pipeline, unpack_model, CANONICAL_ORDER etc. without underscores. For 1.0, either underscore/prune these or document what users may rely on; an __all__ would fix the star-import surface in one line. (hyp.io is fine: load/save/lsl_stream resolve to functions and hyp.load is hyp.io.load.)
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "ns={}; exec('from hypertools import *', ns); print(sorted(k for k in ns if not k.startswith('_')))\nimport hypertools.datageometry as dg; print(dg.__doc__.strip()[:60])\nimport hypertools.config as c; print(c.version)"
findings.expected: Star-import exposes only the supported API; internal modules underscored or documented
findings.actual: star-import names include 'config','core','datageometry','external','tools'; datageometry doc: 'INTERNAL -- not part of the public API.'; config.version: <function version at 0x...> (importlib.metadata.version)

findings.title: apply_model's list-pipeline cannot resolve manip/align/predict/impute names that hypertools.Pipeline resolves ('ZScore' works in Pipeline, fails in apply_model); Pipeline(str) iterates characters
findings.description: hyp.Pipeline(['ZScore', 'PCA']).fit_transform(x) works (the Pipeline resolver checks the manip registry per GH #153), but hyp.apply_model(x, ['ZScore', {'model': 'PCA', ...}]) raises "ValueError: unknown model 'ZScore'; supported names: AffinityPropagation, ..." because apply_model resolves against supported_models() (31 sklearn-style reduce/cluster names only -- no manipulators, aligners, forecasters, imputers). Two documented pipeline mechanisms resolve the same spec string differently. Related rough edge: hyp.Pipeline('ZScore') (string instead of list) iterates the STRING and fails with "ValueError: unknown pipeline step 'Z'; supported names: ..." -- cryptic for a common mistake; should say steps must be a list.
findings.expected: apply_model list pipelines resolve the same registry names as hypertools.Pipeline; Pipeline(str) says 'steps must be a list'
findings.actual: (30, 5); apply_model: unknown model 'ZScore'; supported names: AffinityPropagation, Agglomerati...; Pipeline(str): unknown pipeline step 'Z'; supported names: ...

findings.title: plot(..., predict=..., t=25, return_model=True) bundle forecasts have t+1 rows (26) while hyp.predict(x, t=25) returns t rows (25)
findings.description: The return_model bundle documents "'forecasts': [...] (one forecast array per input dataset...)" under a predict= kwarg documented as 'forecasts `t` new rows per input dataset'. Actual: bundle['predict']['forecasts'][0].shape == (26, 3) for t=25 (bundle['predict']['params'] == {'t': 25}), while the standalone hyp.predict(traj, model='Kalman', t=25) returns (25, 3). The extra row is evidently the seam point prepended so the overlay connects to the trajectory, but the returned DATA should match the documented t rows (or the doc should state t+1 including the last observed point). Any scientist comparing/consuming both paths hits an off-by-one.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; tt=np.linspace(0,6*np.pi,150); traj=np.column_stack([np.sin(tt),np.cos(tt),tt/10]); print(hyp.predict(traj, model='Kalman', t=25).shape); b=hyp.plot(traj, predict='Kalman', t=25, show=False, return_model=True); print(b['predict']['forecasts'][0].shape, b['predict']['params'])"
findings.expected: (25, 3) from both, per 'forecasts t new rows'
findings.actual: predict(t=25) shape: (25, 3); plot bundle forecast shape: (26, 3) | params: {'t': 25}

findings.title: reduce(A, ndims=10) on 5-feature data silently returns 5 dims -- requested dimensionality capped with no warning
findings.description: Asking for more output dimensions than the data has features silently returns the attainable maximum: hyp.reduce(np.random.randn(30,5), ndims=10) -> (30, 5) with no warning or error. A user who requested a 10-dim embedding for a downstream model gets a differently-shaped array without being told. (Contrast: ndims=0/-3/2.5 raise clear ValueErrors -- that validation is good.) A one-line UserWarning ('requested ndims=10 > 5 available features; returning 5') would prevent silent shape surprises.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; print(hyp.reduce(np.random.randn(30,5), ndims=10).shape)"
findings.expected: (30, 10) or a warning/error naming the cap
findings.actual: (30, 5) silently

findings.title: Dependency deprecation leakage: every default MDS run emits two sklearn FutureWarnings; every manip/ZScore call exercises a deprecated pandas 'copy' keyword inside datawrangler
findings.description: hyp.reduce(x, reduce='MDS'-style dict) with hypertools defaults emits sklearn FutureWarnings visible to end users by default: "The default value of `n_init` will change from 4 to 1 in 1.9" and "The default value of `init` will change from 'random' to 'classical_mds' in 1.10" (sklearn/manifold/_mds.py:744/754) -- hypertools should pin these defaults in its MDS spec. Separately, every hyp.manip / ZScore transform triggers "DeprecationWarning: The copy keyword is deprecated ... Copy-on-Write" from datawrangler/decorate/decorate.py:421 (hidden by default warning filters but shown under pytest/-W default) -- meaning hypertools' core data path calls a pandas API scheduled for REMOVAL; when pandas drops the keyword, manip breaks. Needs an upstream datawrangler fix or a version pin before 1.0.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -W default -c "import warnings, numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always'); hyp.manip(np.random.randn(20,4))
print([f'{x.category.__name__}@{x.filename.split(chr(47))[-1]}:{x.lineno}' for x in w])
hyp.reduce(np.random.randn(20,4), reduce='MDS', ndims=2)"
findings.expected: No dependency deprecation warnings on plain default usage
findings.actual: ['DeprecationWarning@decorate.py:421'] (The copy keyword is deprecated...); FutureWarning: The default value of `n_init` will change from 4 to 1 in 1.9 (sklearn _mds.py:744) + init FutureWarning (:754)

findings.description: describe.py's matplotlib branch uses sns.lineplot(units='trace', estimator=None) -- every individual curve is the same color with no legend (see W6_describe.png: three indistinguishable blue lines) -- while the plotly branch adds one named trace per dataset ('dataset 0', 'dataset 1', ...) with showlegend=True when >1 dataset. findings.title: align model='hyper' is documented as a deprecated alias but emits no DeprecationWarning (unlike align='s kwarg alias and legacy dicts, which do warn)
findings.description: align()'s docstring: "'HyperAlign' (hyperalignment, Haxby et al. 2011; 'hyper' is a deprecated alias)". Passing model='hyper' runs with NO DeprecationWarning, while the other two documented deprecations in the same function DO warn: align='hyper' kwarg alias warns ('align= is deprecated as a model-spec kwarg name...') and the legacy {'model','params'} dict warns. Deprecated aliases that never warn will never get cleaned up and users never learn the canonical name.
findings.repro:
env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import warnings, numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; X=np.random.randn(30,5); Y=np.random.randn(30,5)
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always'); hyp.align([X,Y], model='hyper')
print([str(x.message)[:60] for x in w if issubclass(x.category, DeprecationWarning)])"
findings.expected: One DeprecationWarning naming 'HyperAlign' as the canonical spelling
findings.actual: [] (no DeprecationWarning recorded)

findings.title: Rough error surfaces on wrong input kinds: 3D array -> leaked sklearn message; tuple container handled by reduce but misparsed by align; load(12345) -> raw os.fspath TypeError; pipeline='str' -> AttributeError
findings.description: (a) hyp.reduce(np.stack([A,B]), ndims=2) and hyp.plot(3d) raise sklearn's "Found array with dim 3, while dim <= 2 is required by IncrementalPCA." -- never says 'pass a LIST of 2D datasets, not a 3D array'. (b) hyp.reduce((A, B)) treats a tuple like a list (works) but hyp.align((A, B)) raises "input has no observations (0 rows)" for the identical container. (c) hyp.load(12345) leaks "TypeError: expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not int" from os internals. (d) hyp.analyze(A, pipeline='notapipeline') / hyp.plot(A, pipeline='nope') raise "AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'transform'" with no mention of the pipeline= kwarg. Each is a reasonable-mistake input whose message neither names the problem nor the fix.

findings.title: cluster() returns a Python list of numpy int32 scalars (flat across stacked datasets); every sibling returns arrays -- and set_interactive_backend accepts bogus backend names without validation
findings.description: (a) hyp.cluster(A) returns a plain Python list of numpy int32 SCALARS (list[30] of 0-d values), and for a list input one flat list over the row-concatenated data (list[60] for two 30-row datasets) -- documented, but the only place in the API where per-observation results come back as a scalar list rather than an ndarray (or per-dataset lists), so downstream .shape/.reshape idioms fail. (b) hyp.set_interactive_backend('NotABackend') succeeds silently at call time; the invalid name only fails later inside some future interactive plot() call, far from the typo. Cheap early validation against matplotlib's known backends would fail fast.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; A=np.random.randn(30,5); lab=hyp.cluster(A); print(type(lab), type(lab[0]), getattr(lab, 'shape', 'no shape')); hyp.set_interactive_backend('NotABackend'); print('bogus backend accepted silently')"
findings.expected: ndarray of labels (or documented consistently); ValueError at set_interactive_backend call time for unknown backends
findings.actual: <class 'list'> <class 'numpy.int32'> no shape; bogus backend accepted silently
